correctness.rationale: Derive coefficientwise commutation equations over the split square-zero coefficient ring. For nonscalar residue A0, its field centralizer is exactly span(I,A0), giving q^(2d+2) for each choice of radical coefficients. For scalar A0, the common centralizer of a d-tuple has dimension 4 if all entries scalar, dimension 2 if all entries lie in the unique two-dimensional commutative algebra generated by a nonscalar entry, and dimension 1 otherwise. These alternatives are disjoint and exhaustive, and the number of such commutative two-dimensional algebras is (q^4-q)/(q^2-q)=q^2+q+1. Counts sum to q^(4d+4) with four positive multiplicities for every d>=2. Exact direct and kernel-count verification completed for p=2,d=1,2 and p=3,d=1; only proof certifies general q,d. Weighted centralizer sum gives the claimed commuting-pair formula and fixed-q limit q^-6 with O_q(q^-2d) remainder.

value.rationale: The full distribution of element-centralizer sizes is an intrinsic finite-ring invariant; the explicit four-level spectrum for every nonprincipal embedding dimension d>=2 is a natural complete classification not covered by the known principal length-two tables. The derived nonzero q^-6 limiting commuting probability has structural explanation from pairs with both reductions scalar. This establishes a motivated boundary between ring-size growth and persistence of commutation, without requiring a conjectural downstream theorem.
